object_description: elongated school bar and shorter sports volume forming a courtyard
design_condition: Two volumes aligned with the surrounding development create a spacious schoolyard, connected to the surroundings by passages and clearly visible through the gap between the buildings.

positive.statement: The calm urban-planning response is convincing in its consistency from the basic approach through to the architectural formulation.
The two volumes create a clear urban structure and external spatial hierarchy with simple means.
The hall forms a prominent communication space between school and city.
The entrances and access organization provide good orientation and are operationally convenient and efficient.
The classrooms are well proportioned and the teaching areas are organized clearly.
The restrained material and window strategy supports a calm architectural integration.
The compact building and durable materials support good energy performance and resource efficiency.
The project has good overall economic efficiency and low floor area and volume.

negative.statement: The bicycle racks in the important passage and the fragile courtyard glasshouse are questionable.
The covered sports anteroom and rear courtyard offer limited spatial and experiential quality.
The access zone on the school floors is unattractive, cramped, and narrow.
The sports area is clearly organized but its dimensions are too tight.
The direction of the structural ribs does not follow the flow of forces.
The need for ribbed ceilings is questioned for cost reasons.
The basement combination does not provide a convincing added value between the school and sports buildings.
The project lacks a more comprehensive idea for the urban development of the district and the plot.
